items.title: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope To Sign With 76ers After Buyout With Grizzlies
items.originalTitle: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope To Sign With 76ers After Buyout With Grizzlies
items.headlineZh: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope To 签约动向更新
items.titleZh: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope To 签约动向更新
items.summary:
Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has agreed to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and plans to sign a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers once he clears waivers. The Grizzlies and Caldwell-Pope's agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, finalized the buyout Saturday.

The move gives Philadelphia a veteran wing shooter and defender just one day after the team signed LeBron James. Caldwell-Pope, a two-time NBA champion, won his first title with the Lakers in 2020 alongside James during the league's bubble format before capturing a second ring with the Denver Nuggets in 2023.

Caldwell-Pope, 33, underwent surgery in February to address a misalignment in his right pinkie finger, sidelining him for the final 31 games of last season. Before the injury, he averaged 8.4 points, 2.7 assists, 2.5 rebounds and 21.3 minutes across 51 games with Memphis, marking his lowest scoring and minutes averages since his rookie season. He shot 49.5 percent on two-point attempts and 31.6 percent from three-point range.

Caldwell-Pope has long been regarded as one of the league's top 3-and-D players, though his three-point shooting has declined in recent seasons. After shooting at least 39 percent from beyond the arc every season from 2020 to 2024, he has failed to top 34.2 percent over the past two seasons.

items.headlineZh: Had No Interest 相关消息更新
items.titleZh: Had No Interest 相关消息更新
items.summary:
There had been reporting that LeBron James was interesting in teaming up with one of his former teammates when he picked a new team. The Golden State Warriors and Cleveland Cavaliers were linked to Anthony Davis and Kyrie Irving, respectively.

However, neither Davis' current team, the Washington Wizards, nor Irving's current team, the Dallas Mavericks, had any interest in trading either player. In addition, James, nor his agent Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, made no demands of teams that they must trade for Davis or Irving to get the NBA's all-time leading scorer.

Ultimately, James picked the Philadelphia 76ers for the upcoming season. It's expected that both Davis and Irving will start the season with the Wizards and Mavericks, respectively.

With their pursuit of LeBron James having come up short, the Golden State Warriors are expected to pivot to re-signing Draymond Green. The expectation is the Green will re-sign at a figure close to the $28 million player option that he opted out of at the beginning of the offseason.

items.summary:
The Cleveland Cavaliers and Golden State Warriors are showing interest in signing Mario Hezonja. The veteran wing recently informed Real Madrid that he intends to return to the NBA after spending the last six seasons in Europe.

Hezonja played five seasons in the NBA for the Orlando Magic, New York Knicks and Portland Trail Blazers. The 6-foot-8 wing then played a season apiece in Greece and Russia, before spending the last four years with Real Madrid.

Last season, Hezonja averaged 15 points, 4.3 rebounds and 2.1 assists. The 31-year-old shot 44.4% from the floor over 80 games across EuroLeague and domestic competitions.

items.title: Jonathan Kuminga, Cavaliers Have Mutual Interest
items.originalTitle: Jonathan Kuminga, Cavaliers Have Mutual Interest
items.headlineZh: Jonathan Kuminga 相关消息更新
items.titleZh: Jonathan Kuminga 相关消息更新
items.summary:
The Cleveland Cavaliers have maintained contact with free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga and his agent throughout LeBron James' free agency, with mutual interest existing between the two sides.

Kuminga, 23, became a free agent after the Atlanta Hawks declined their $24.3 million option on his contract. He averaged 12.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and shot 33 percent from three-point range across 36 games split between Atlanta and the Golden State Warriors last season.

Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, described his client's affinity for Cleveland in a brief interview.

"Jonathan likes the Cavs, likes (coach) Kenny Atkinson, and (star) Donovan Mitchell likes him," said Turner, noting that Kuminga trained in Cleveland for two months last summer.

Kuminga also has a prior relationship with Atkinson from the coach's time as a Golden State assistant under Steve Kerr.

The financial structure of any deal remains complicated. Cleveland could offer Kuminga roughly $6 million using cap space it would have otherwise directed toward James, or theoretically up to $15 million through a salary cap exception, though doing so would significantly limit what the team could offer unsigned veteran James Harden. The Cavaliers and Harden have intentionally left his new contract unfinalized to preserve roster flexibility, with a two- or three-year deal expected once Cleveland's broader plans take shape.

Kuminga, however, is believed to prefer a sign-and-trade involving Atlanta, which would allow him to earn closer to the $20 million to $23 million range he would have received had the Hawks exercised his option.

Both Cleveland and the Los Angeles Lakers have been linked to Kuminga as sign-and-trade candidates, though sources indicated the Lakers' potential trade package is considered underwhelming compared to what Cleveland could offer. The Cavaliers have been connected to possible trades involving veteran forward Max Strus and point guard Dennis Schroder as part of a potential deal. Any sign-and-trade would require Cleveland to remain under the NBA's roughly $209 million first apron, which is part of why Harden's new contract has not yet been finalized. Kuminga could also return to Atlanta on a short-term deal, with the Los Angeles Clippers and Milwaukee Bucks mentioned as additional potential destinations.

Cleveland reached the Eastern Conference finals for the first time since 2018 last season before being swept by the eventual champion New York Knicks. The team has since lost forward Dean Wade to Philadelphia, guard Keon Ellis to Brooklyn and forward Larry Nance Jr. to Indiana in free agency, in addition to missing out on James.

"There isn't much left out there," said a league source with knowledge of the Cavaliers' thinking. "They have to get their young guys ready to play."

Cleveland's young players include third-year wing Jaylon Tyson, who broke out last season, second-year guard Tyrese Proctor and rookie Meleek Thomas, the team's second-round pick who was named among the top players at NBA Summer League in Las Vegas.

items.title: LeBron James Could Play At Least Two More Seasons After Nearly Retiring This Offseason
items.originalTitle: LeBron James Could Play At Least Two More Seasons After Nearly Retiring This Offseason
items.headlineZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 Could 相关消息更新
items.titleZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 Could 相关消息更新
items.summary:
While LeBron James says he came close to retirement this offseason, he ultimately decided to continue his career and will sign a two-year contract with the Philadelphia 76ers. James could play both seasons and put off retirement until at least 2028.

"And my understanding is there's a real chance here he plays both of these years," said Shams Charania.

James said that he was leaning towards retirement when the Los Angeles Lakers were eliminated by the Oklahoma City Thunder in the second round of the playoffs.

"I thought I was done when the season ended," wrote James on X. "I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love truly love this game, and I have more to give."

There have been conflicting reports over the years on whether James would announce his retirement plans in advance to have a farewell tour, or if it would come suddenly.

James will turn 42 in December.
items.oneLineZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 Could 相关消息更新
items.displayTitle: LeBron James Could Play At Least Two More Seasons After Nearly Retiring This Offseason

items.title: Heat Shift Focus To DeMar DeRozan After Losing Out On LeBron James
items.originalTitle: Heat Shift Focus To DeMar DeRozan After Losing Out On LeBron James
items.headlineZh: 热火 Shift Focus 相关消息更新
items.titleZh: 热火 Shift Focus 相关消息更新
items.summary:
The Miami Heat are expected to renew talks with free agent DeMar DeRozan after LeBron James chose the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday. Miami and DeRozan have held mutual interest in the past, and fresh conversations are anticipated now that James is off the market.

DeRozan averaged 18.4 points on 49.7 percent shooting across 77 starts for the Sacramento Kings last season, adding 4.1 assists and 2.1 rebounds per game.

A veteran Eastern Conference scout offered a candid assessment of DeRozan's potential fit in Miami.

"He's had years in San Antonio where he passed it more," said the scout. "He's a midrange guy and on a given night, he can get you points. He doesn't do much else. If he accepted the role off the bench, and then finishes the game, he could be fine."

DeRozan would give Miami a high-scoring option off the bench, though starting him alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo would create spacing concerns given all three players' limitations from three-point range. If DeRozan signs, the Heat would likely still need to add a dedicated three-point shooter elsewhere on the roster.

Heat president Pat Riley reiterated the team's priorities in comments to Dan Le Batard this week, emphasizing playmaking over shooting as the more urgent need.

"Everybody talks about shooting; that's not the main priority right now," said Riley. "It's another playmaker."

ESPN's Shams Charania indicated Friday that DeRozan and free agent Bradley Beal represent Miami's most realistic remaining targets following James' decision.

"Now they will now shift their focus to players like Demar DeRozan, Bradley Beal," said Charania. "Could you find a player like Klay Thompson on the buyout market?"

Miami currently has 12 players on standard contracts, three shy of the maximum roster size, and operates under a $209 million hard cap that limits its financial flexibility to add multiple significant contributors this offseason.

items.title: LeBron James Looked For Cavs To Trade For Kyrie Irving
items.originalTitle: LeBron James Looked For Cavs To Trade For Kyrie Irving
items.headlineZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 Looked 交易影响继续发酵
items.titleZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 Looked 交易影响继续发酵
items.summary:
LeBron James had been pushing for former teammate Kyrie Irving to join him in a potential return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, according to league sources. The Dallas Mavericks, however, have shown no interest in engaging the Cavaliers on a trade, and Irving is believed to be comfortable remaining where he is.

That reported effort adds another layer to James' complicated free agency decision, one that continues to weigh a possible third stint in Cleveland against a return to the Miami Heat, where he won two championships and two MVP awards from 2010 to 2014.

Cleveland's roster already features high-usage playmakers in Donovan Mitchell and James Harden, meaning James' addition alone likely wouldn't resolve the team's most pressing need. The Cavaliers' actual weakness lies up front where Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley struggled to hold ground during their conference finals loss to the eventual champion New York Knicks.

Miami, by contrast, presents a more straightforward opportunity for James at this stage of his career. The Heat recently acquired two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo, and pairing James with Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo would allow him to slot into a complementary role rather than shoulder primary playmaking duties, something he last did successfully during the 2019-20 season with the Lakers.

A former teammate told ESPN that James, soon to turn 42, no longer needs this final stretch of his career to be defined by another championship.

"To be the GOAT, you got to win championships, etc. Now that's settled," said the former teammate. "Now it's about his joy, his happiness. If it ends in a championship, great. But he won't be defined by how this ends."

That same source suggested Miami would allow James to focus purely on playing basketball without added pressure.

"He can play freely," said the source. "He can be Tom Brady late in his career, not worrying about being the hero."

Forward Mouhamadou Gueye is set to join Valencia Basket in Spain for the upcoming season. The Spanish club even announced the addition of Gueye, despite the 6-foot-9 forward not having been waived by the Charlotte Hornets yet.

Gueye finished last season with the Chicago Bulls. He's also played for the Toronto Raptors in the NBA, as well as four different G League franchises.

In order to satisfy trade rules as part of the four-team trade between the Bulls, Hornets, Brooklyn Nets and Minnesota Timberwolves, Gueye was sent from Chicago to Charlotte. The Hornets are expected to waive Gueye, as the team is facing a roster crunch.

items.titleZh: Open To Signing 签约动向更新
items.summary:
The Golden State Warriors are open to signing a one or two-year extension with Steph Curry, according to Anthony Slater of ESPN.

Curry will be extension-eligible on August 29.

"If he wants a one-year extension at big money, if he wants a two-year extension - the Warriors are very open to that conversation.

"I think they want to see how this roster looks in the short-term and long-term, and by the time we get to late August when he's eligible, Steph Curry and the Warriors will sit down and decide," said Slater.

Curry is currently on a one-year, $62 million deal.

It was reported last week that the Warriors still need to add another star in order to have a shot at signing LeBron James.

items.originalTitle: LeBron James May Remain Genuinely Undecided On Free Agency Decision
items.headlineZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 May 签约动向更新
items.titleZh: 勒布朗·詹姆斯 May 签约动向更新
items.summary:
LeBron James still had not announced a decision on his next team, 24 days after confirming he would not return to the Los Angeles Lakers fort he 2026-27 season. A source close to James offered a candid assessment of the situation.

"Nobody knows right now except LeBron," the source told The Athletic. "And I'm not even sure LeBron knows."

The prolonged wait has left the Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat, Minnesota Timberwolves and Philadelphia 76ers all in limbo as they wait to see whether James will sign or whether they need to pivot toward strengthening their rosters elsewhere. James addressed the timeline last Thursday during an appearance at Fanatics Fest in New York.

"I won't hold you guys up too much longer," said James.

James' agent, Rich Paul, has said he has already communicated everything necessary to the five teams considered front-runners for James' services. Paul addressed his approach during an appearance on his own podcast this week.

"Is there anything more we should be doing? We could be doing?" said Paul. "No. We don't need you to go above and beyond about anything. We understand it. It's clear. All the messages have been sent."

Speculation has continued to swirl in the absence of concrete information, including reports of a since-deleted Heat YouTube link referencing a July 27 press conference, which the team described as an honest mistake. Sources close to James also dismissed rumors that he had reversed a prior decision, calling those claims false.

Only two teams have made roster moves directly tied to pursuing James. Warriors forward Draymond Green, also represented by Paul, declined his player option in late June in coordination with Golden State's front office to create flexibility for potentially signing James and trading for Anthony Davis. Sources said there were no guarantees attached to that move. Meanwhile, James Harden has remained unsigned as part of a plan to preserve Cleveland's ability to sign James, a strategy Harden has publicly confirmed as the team's goal.

items.title: Jordan Walsh, Celtics Agree To Three-Year, $16M Extension
items.originalTitle: Jordan Walsh, Celtics Agree To Three-Year, $16M Extension
items.headlineZh: Jordan Walsh 签约动向更新
items.titleZh: Jordan Walsh 签约动向更新
items.summary:
Jordan Walsh and the Boston Celtics have agreed to a three-year, $16 million contract extension. The deal will begin with the 2027-28 season as the Celtics previously picked up their 2026-27 option on him in June. Walsh is represented by Ramon Sessions.

Walsh appeared in 68 games last season with the Celtics, averaging 5.4 points and 4.0 rebounds in 68 minutes.

Walsh was the 38th overall pick in the 2023 draft out of Arkansas.

Walsh is now signed through 2030 and joins Neemias Queta with a multi-year extension this offseason with the Celtics.

items.titleZh: 雷霆将吕冈茨·多尔特送至老鹰
items.summary:
The Atlanta Hawks will not immediately pursue contract extension talks with Lu Dort, sources told Jake Fischer and Marc Stein of The Stein Line.

Dort is entering the final year of current deal worth nearly $18 million.

It has been noted by multiple executives around the league that the Hawks have several mid-tier salaries they could flip for a star.

Jonathan Kuminga is also reportedly open to a short-term deal with the Hawks. The Hawks could sign-and-trade Kuminga, but they will be choosy as to what team they trade with.

items.title: Rockets Sign Isaiah Crawford To Contract
items.originalTitle: Rockets Sign Isaiah Crawford To Contract
items.headlineZh: 火箭签下 Isaiah Crawford To
items.titleZh: 火箭签下 Isaiah Crawford To
items.summary:
The Houston Rockets have re-signed forward Isaiah Crawford.

Crawford appeared in 14 games as a two-way player for the Rockets in 2025-26, averaging 11.0 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.2 blocks per 36 minutes played. He recorded career highs of 11 points and 6 rebounds in the season finale vs. Memphis on April 12.

In 20 games while transferred to the Rockets G League affiliate, Rio Grande Valley, Crawford averaged 19.0 ppg, 7.6 rpg, 3.1 apg and 2.1 spg while shooting 51.5% from the floor and 39.2% from 3-point range.

Crawford was was a two-way player for Sacramento in 2024-25 and helped its G League affiliate, Stockton, win the championship.
